culturalBackground: Mandala means circle in Sanskrit, and mandala mehndi is built from rings of petals and patterns around a central point.
A mandala in the centre of the palm or the back of the hand is one of the most recognisable mehndi layouts.
In Indian and Pakistani mehndi, this round design is commonly called a tikki or gol tikki.
The design depends on symmetry: each ring repeats the same shape all the way around.
applicationTips: Start with a small circle in the centre and add one ring at a time.
Turn the hand, not the cone, as you work around the circle to keep the petals even.
Finish with a ring of dots; it hides small unevenness in the outer edge.

faqPool.q: What does mandala mean in mehndi?
faqPool.a: It refers to a circular design built from repeating rings around a centre point.

faqPool.q: Is a mandala the same as a tikki design?
faqPool.a: A tikki is a round mandala placed on the palm or back of the hand, usually with decorated fingertips.

faqPool.q: Are mandala designs suitable for beginners?
faqPool.a: Yes. A basic mandala uses only circles, petals and dots, and it can be made more detailed as you improve.
